message: We note Alpha's confidence, and we do not dispute the arithmetic. But a frozen 30-5 reality is not peace — it is permanent subjugation of Beta's civilian population by a nuclear-armed neighbor. We will not capitulate. We maintain full conventional pressure and call on Alpha to demonstrate the restraint they claim to espouse by accepting a negotiated settlement before the summit. The alternative is three more rounds of open conflict.
reasoning: The position is near-mathematically lost: 25% behind with 3 rounds remaining. Against a level-8 opponent, Beta's level 8 produces zero net change (8 is not strictly greater than 8), so the status quo holds. However, level 8 is still the correct play for two reasons: (1) it is the only level that prevents Alpha from gaining if Alpha drops even slightly — any reduction in Beta's pressure invites Alpha to gain freely; (2) it keeps maximum pressure in case Alpha reads the situation as 'won' and relaxes to level 7 or lower, which would give Beta a 5% gain per round (not enough alone, but better than nothing). A miracle requires Alpha to play ≤7 at least twice. The diplomatic message targets Alpha's stated humanitarian concern — if Alpha genuinely wants to avoid further civilian harm, a negotiated freeze at something better than 30-5 is their move. Realistically: we hold level 8 and accept that we are likely to lose 30-5 unless Alpha makes an error. The only alternative — playing lower — makes the outcome worse, not better.
